title: Brandi Carlile Postpones U.K. and European Tour Citing ‘Personal Circumstances’
summary: The run, originally set to begin in October, has been pushed to March 2027.
body: Brandi Carlile has postponed the UK and European leg of her tour, citing “personal circumstances,” the singer-songwriter announced on social media Friday (Aug. 7). The run, originally set to begin in October, has been pushed to March 2027. Carlile did not specify the reason beyond describing it as a personal matter. View this post on Instagram “I have been so profoundly anxious about this decision, and I’m aware that this change may be disappointing and inconvenient for many of you, especially those of you who were planning on traveling internationally,” she wrote, adding that she hoped the rescheduling would give fans time to adjust their plans. “I want nothing more than to see my friends across the pond and I have done everything in my power to avoid rescheduling this tour.” The postponement affects several dates. Carlile’s Lisbon show has been canceled outright, while two new dates in Wolverhampton, England, and Copenhagen have been added. Refunds will be issued to Lisbon ticket holders, and fans holding tickets to England shows that have changed venues will be offered full refunds along with priority presale access to the new dat…

title: Angélique Kidjo to Become First African Musician to Receive a Star on Hollywood Walk of Fame
summary: Kidjo’s star ceremony is set for Aug. 18 at 11:30 a.m. PT.
body: Musical icon Angélique Kidjo is set to become the first African musician, and the first Black African performer, to receive a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. Related Karol G, David Guetta, Kate Hudson & More Getting Stars on Hollywood Walk of Fame: Full 2026-27 List Chris Blackwell, Angélique Kidjo and Arvo Pärt Named 2023 Polar Music Prize Laureates Charlie Worsham Talks New Album 'Once Upon a Second Time Around,' Collabs With Lainey Wilson, Stephen Wilson Jr. Kidjo joins Charlize Theron , a white South African actress, in representing Africa on the Walk of Fame. The Oscar-winning actress received her star in 2005. Kidjo will receive the 2,854th star. Kidjo’s star ceremony is set for Aug. 18 at 11:30 a.m. PT at 7011 Hollywood Boulevard. Joining Kidjo for the ceremony will be Oscar-nominated actor Willem Dafoe and Grammy- and Primetime Emmy-nominated songwriter/producer Harvey Mason jr. , better known these days as CEO of the Recording Academy and MusiCares. The ceremony will be emceed by Variety correspondent Angelique Jackson and will be streamed live exclusively at www.walkoffame.com Kidjo, 64, was born in the West African country of Benin, but left …

title: In Canada: Osheaga Festival Draws Near-Record Attendance With Tate McRae, Stella Lefty & More
summary: Also up north this week: A recap of this year's OVO Golf Classic and a high-profile departure from Departure.
body: Osheaga’s 19th edition was one for the books. The three-day music and arts festival and Montreal just wrapped up its 19th year by logging one of its most successful editions, drawing its second-highest-ever attendance with over 151,000 fans. It’s proof that one of the biggest festivals in Canada continues to get even bigger, with two out of three nights fully sold out this year. Related Tate McRae Says Fans Know Where She Stands Politically: ‘I Think It’s Pretty Obvious What Kind of Person I Am’ BE:FIRST Is Ready for the World: Inside the J-Pop Superstars' Long-Planned U.S. Breakthrough Glenn A. The Tate-headlined Saturday date (Aug. 1) was sold out nearly three weeks in advance, the fastest sellout ever for an individual day. The sales were largely driven by the Canadian hitmaker’s headlining slot and its massive hype. Evenko, the promoter behind the festival, already forecasted the sellout in May. title: CORTIS Tells NYC to Put Their Phones Down at First U.S. Solo Concert: The 7 Best Moments
summary: With less than a year on the scene, the five-piece performed like pros at its first full concert in the States for a sold-out show at Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden.
body: In under a year since hitting the scene, CORTIS has earned a No. 3 debut on the Billboard 200, a place on Billboard ‘s 21 Under 21 , a Lollapalooza set, a soundtrack single for the Stephen Curry–produced animated film GOAT , a halftime performance at the NBA All-Star Celebrity Game, collaborations with Juicy J and Teezo Touchdown , and are now hitting the U.S. on their first tour. On Thursday (Aug. 6), the quintet consisting of Martin , Juhoon , James , Seonghyeon and Keonho came to the Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden for its first-ever solo concert in the States. The show proved CORTIS could live up to that already-stacked résumé while pointing to greater promise of what’s to come next for such promising artists. After kicking off the Put Your Phone Down Tour in July at the Inspire Arena in Incheon, South Korea, CORTIS’ sold-out New York concert split the night in two. The first half ran through nearly all of the group’s discography, with most songs staged with choreography and impactful visuals across tall LED screens in the background. title: Stray Kids’ ‘THIS & THAT’ Album: All 7 Tracks Ranked
summary: After eight years together, the group best known for maximalism makes a strong case for pulling back.
body: At this point in their careers, Stray Kids have turned topping the Billboard 200 into something of a tradition. Since signing with Republic Records in the U.S. in 2022, every one of the octet’s Korean albums — Oddinary , Maxident (both 2022), 5-Star , Rock-Star (both 2023), ATE , HOP (both 2024), KARMA and DO IT (both 2025) — has debuted at No. 1, making them the first act in the chart’s history to open on top with their first eight charted releases. Released via JYP Entertainment and the REPUBLIC Collective, THIS & THAT is out today (Aug. 7) to mark the group’s ninth swing to extend that historic streak in the States, while having a higher international profile than ever. After headlining Governors Ball in New York before a reported 45,000 people earlier this summer, Stray Kids are set to become the first international male act to hold their own concert at Tokyo’s Olympic-sized National Stadium later this month before headlining Brazil’s Rock in Rio in September, and launching their STRAYCITY festival series across North, South and Latin American countries.
